summary: Cohort split and intermittent legacy-model routing during atomic rollout handshake
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported mixed outputs and occasional routing to an older model variant for a single tenant during a scheduled canary rollout. The tenant is explicitly pinned to a new model via the tenant-level pin API, but ~2-3% of requests observed over a 30-minute window were served by the legacy model.

Impact:
- Affects a production tenant (Acme Health) on enterprise plan.
- Incorrect model responses cause downstream QA failures and a temporary halt to a clinical inference workflow.
- Customer reported latency spikes coincident with misrouted responses.

Timeline (high level):
- 2024-05-11 09:00 UTC: Canary rollout initiated for redwood/open-13B-v2 -> new revision r2024-05-11.
- 2024-05-11 09:07 UTC: Control plane writes rollout snapshot; orchestrator starts slice-prewarm.
- 2024-05-11 09:12 UTC: Edge prewarm completed; tenant pin applied via pin API (confirmed by pin service).
- 2024-05-11 09:20-09:50 UTC: Customer observed intermittent legacy-model responses and raised this ticket.

Initial hypothesis:
- An ordering race between the atomic rollout handshake and edge session token rotation caused a cohort split: some edge nodes accepted the new snapshot but retained an older affinity mapping, causing requests from the same tenant to be routed to different variants.

Steps to reproduce (attempted):
1) Create a test tenant and explicitly pin to a new model revision.
2) Initiate a phased canary rollout with shadow prewarm and 5% traffic slice.
3) Trigger rapid edge reconnects by cycling a subset of edge proxies (simulated network blips).
4) Observe request routing and session affinity over 10k requests.

Observed logs and metrics:
- Edge proxy logs show 'pin-ack' sent at 09:12:14 UTC from control plane, but a subset of proxies show 'session-affinity: legacy' entries for the same tenant until 09:18 UTC.
- Orchestrator logs show a partial snapshot commit to 6/8 routing shards during the handshake window.
- Tenant request traces from the customer show mixed model IDs in response headers (x-model-id: redwood/open-13B-v1 and x-model-id: redwood/open-13B-v2).

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Applied per-tenant forced-commit: re-assert pin via admin API (pin-override=true) and drain edge sessions for the tenant. This reduced mismatches to <0.1% within 7 minutes.
- Advised customer to pause batch-critical inference runs until full rollout stabilization.
steps_to_reproduce: See description steps; repro requires canary rollout + simulated edge reconnects + explicit tenant pinning

investigation_notes: Repro: Deterministic when edge proxies are force-cycled during handshake window; non-deterministic without simulated blips.
Control-plane currently treats replica commit as majority-based for speed; this yields a short window where some routing shards serve legacy mappings.
Pinned tenants should be treated with strict commit semantics (full shard commit) to avoid cohort split; current optimization bypasses that.
Related to previous SUP-4721 (canary fallback misroute) but different failure mode: this is handshake/quorum ordering rather than cache TTL.
Telemetry indicates affected tenant saw ~72 mismatched requests across 30 minutes before intervention; latency correlated with mismatch events (+120ms median).
Proposed immediate mitigation: for pinned tenants, require coordinator to wait for all shard confirmations OR apply a fast-path flush of affinity mapping to edge proxies after commit.
resolution: Workaround: support executed a forced pin-commit and tenant edge drain which mitigated impact for Acme Health. Permanent fix: control-plane patch landed in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/1894 to change handshake for pinned tenants to require full-shard convergence; additional edge flush RPC added (control-plane v1.22.3). Planned release: 2024-05-15 canary, 2024-05-16 full rollout. Post-release verification: run scripted edge-cycle repro and confirm zero mismatches across 100k requests. Follow-ups: add metric for 'pinned-tenant-cohort-split' and update canary runbook to include edge-drain step for pinned tenants.

public_communication: Customer was notified of workaround and planned fix on 2024-05-14. Post-release we will provide an incident summary and recommended best practices for tenant pinning during rollouts.
closure_criteria: Control-plane patch deployed and verified in canary and prod with zero mismatches in scripted repro; customer confirms incident resolved and signs off.
